title: Why does popcorn pop?
sources: Purdue University Department of Food Science

lines.text: Why does popcorn explode into fluffy white clouds when heated, while sweet corn just burns?
lines.caps: Why does *popcorn pop | while sweet corn *burns?

lines.text: Popcorn kernels have an extraordinarily tough, waterproof outer hull called the pericarp.
Inside each kernel sits a tiny droplet of water surrounded by hard, dense starch.
lines.caps: Inside sits a *droplet of water | surrounded by *starch

lines.text: When you heat the kernel past four hundred degrees, that trapped water turns into high-pressure steam.
The steam cooks the dense starch into a molten, gelatinous hot dough.
lines.caps: Cooks the starch into a *molten | gelatinous *dough

lines.text: When internal pressure reaches one hundred and thirty-five pounds per square inch, the hull violently explodes.
lines.caps: At 135 PSI the hull *explodes | turning inside *out!

lines.text: As it bursts, the molten starch instantly cools into the delicious crunchy snack you love.
lines.caps: Instant cooling creates the *crunchy snack | you *love!
